questions.question_en: According to Fajan's rules, which of the following is not correct about covalent character?
Consider the following pairs: Order — Property. A) NO₂ > O₃ > H₂O — Bond angle. B) HF > H₂O > NH₃ — Dipole moment. C) I₂ > F₂ > N₂ — Bond length. Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
An open vessel containing air was heated from 27 °C to 727 °C. Some air was expelled. What is the fraction of air remaining in the vessel? (Assume air as an ideal gas)
questions.note: By the ideal gas law at constant P and V, n2/n1 = T1/T2 = 300/1000 = 3/10, so the fraction of air REMAINING should be 3/10 (option 3) and the fraction EXPELLED should be 7/10. The paper marks option 2 (7/10) as correct even though the question asks for the fraction remaining. Recorded the marked option per instructions; the official key appears to answer the fraction expelled instead of the fraction remaining.

Identify the correct statements from the following. A) At 298 K, the potential of hydrogen electrode placed in a solution of pH = 10, is −0.59 V. B) The limiting molar conductivity of Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻ is 119 and 76 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively. The limiting molar conductivity of CaCl₂ is 195 S cm² mol⁻¹. C) The correct relationship between Kc and Ecell⊖ is Ecell⊖ = (2.303RT/nF) log Kc

For a first order reaction, a plot of ln k (y-axis) and 1/T (x-axis) gave the straight line with slope equal to −10³k and intercept equal to 2.303 (on y-axis). What is the activation energy (Ea in kJ mol⁻¹) of the reaction? (Given R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹)
questions.note: The printed slope value reads as "−10³k" with a lowercase italic k (matching the style of "ln k" elsewhere in the same question) rather than a capital K for Kelvin; it is almost certainly meant to be the numeral −10³ (units K, since the x-axis is 1/T), which is consistent with the marked answer (Ea = 1000 × R = 8314 J/mol = 8.314 kJ/mol). Transcribed the character as it visually appears in the source image.
